discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
rationale: Topological insulators are a foundational, long-matured condensed-matter breakthrough that has long been tipped for the prize. The 2016 prize covered topological phases only in a general way and left this discovery unrewarded. Kane and Mele predicted the Z2 quantum spin Hall insulator in 2005, and Molenkamp confirmed it in HgTe quantum wells in 2007. The trio fits the Nobel pattern of pairing theory with experiment, and all three have already received major precursor prizes such as the Breakthrough, Dirac and Oliver Buckley awards.
